facts.statement: India and Pakistan signed the Indus Waters Treaty on 19 September 1960, with the World Bank as a signatory.
facts.source: World Bank, Fact Sheet: The Indus Waters Treaty 1960 and the Role of the World Bank
facts.note: Not opened from the build session (official sites were not reachable); check it against the link.

facts.statement: Under the treaty the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas and Sutlej) are for India’s use and the western rivers (Indus, Jhelum and Chenab) for Pakistan’s, with some uses allowed to India.
facts.source: World Bank, Fact Sheet: The Indus Waters Treaty 1960 and the Role of the World Bank
facts.note: Not opened from the build session (official sites were not reachable); check it against the link.

facts.statement: India said on 23 April 2025 that it would hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance.
facts.source: Ministry of External Affairs of India, press releases
facts.note: Find the MEA briefing of 23 April 2025 and check its wording.

facts.statement: Pakistan’s National Security Committee said on 24 April 2025 that it rejected India’s step and that the treaty could not be suspended by one side.
facts.note: Find the National Security Committee statement of 24 April 2025 and check its wording.
